overview: Both are blotting techniques for detecting specific nucleic acid sequences, differing only in whether the target is DNA or RNA.
genZNote: Southern blot hunts for DNA. Northern blot hunts for RNA. (Named after the scientist and a geography pun, not compass directions.)

aspects.label: Target Molecule
aspects.valueA: DNA fragments, typically after restriction digestion.
aspects.valueB: RNA, usually mRNA, to study gene expression.

aspects.label: Typical Use
aspects.valueA: Detecting specific DNA sequences, gene mapping, paternity/forensic testing.
aspects.valueB: Studying gene expression levels — which genes are being transcribed and how much.

aspects.label: Origin of Name
aspects.valueA: Named after its inventor, Edwin Southern.
aspects.valueB: A play on 'Southern', naming the RNA version 'Northern' by direction.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Western blot (for proteins) completes the trio — Southern (DNA), Northern (RNA), Western (protein).
overlay.memoryTrick: Southern = Sir Edwin Southern = DNA. Northern (opposite direction) = RNA.
overlay.commonMisconception: These blots are not named for any geographic or biological logic beyond the original pun — 'Northern' and 'Western' were invented as jokes on 'Southern'.
